review.summary: Chunk `target-filtering` (crates/scm-sdk/src/airs/red_team/targets.rs + crates/scm-sdk/tests/red_team_management_contracts.rs) delivers its declared scope correctly and with real, verifiable evidence. `TargetListOptions::profiling_status` is added as an additive optional field on an already `#[non_exhaustive]` struct, validated pre-auth against exactly the vendor `ProfilingStatusFilter` domain (NOT_STARTED, IN_PROGRESS, COMPLETED, FAILED — byte-matching contracts/vendor/red-team-management/0.86.0/openapi.json:5300-5307), and propagated unchanged through list, list_pages, list_items and list_all via the existing `Pages` closure clone. Legacy `status` keeps its old wire behavior (`common::filter` only, no translation), and both fields carry the rustdoc the plan requires, including the narrowed DRAFT/ACTIVE upstream domain, all five de-declared legacy values, the profiling_status migration targets, and an explicit "the service may reject legacy values" caveat — i.e. no implication that local acceptance means upstream acceptance. Security posture is sound: invalid filters fail with ErrorKind::Validation before token acquisition or dispatch (asserted in `invalid_profiling_filter_never_acquires_token_or_dispatches`, which checks provider.calls == 0 and zero transport requests), options are redacted in Debug, and the transport double-checks that no synthetic secret appears in request Debug output. Evidence is executed, not asserted: the attempt-01 receipt (source_sha256 a5f3038…, passed: true) contains the full registered phase-22 command set with exit_code 0, including four real `scripts/check-rust.py` runs (1.89.0/1.99.0 × red-team and red-team+arbitrary_precision, 60–298 s each) whose captured sub-commands include `cargo test --workspace` and `clippy -D warnings`, so both the in-file unit tests and the integration tests actually ran; `tools/red_team_management.py --check --require-through-phase 22` passes and hash-binds targets.rs and the contracts test file plus the two profiling test names into contracts/vendor/red-team-management/0.86.0/operations.json runtimeEvidence. The implementation also matches the pre-existing module idiom (eager pre-validation in list_pages mirrors scans.rs:151). No blocker or high findings. The one substantive gap is maintainability/architecture: the accepted filter domain is an inline string literal in targets.rs with no mechanical binding to the reviewed vendor enum, unlike the data-plane path which validates declared query values through contract.json via `common::current_query`; a reviewed upstream enum extension could leave the SDK silently rejecting a newly declared value. Two low findings concern documentation of the response-only INIT value and end-to-end coverage of only one of the four accepted filter values.

findings.description: The accepted profiling filter domain is a hand-written inline literal set (`matches!(value.as_str(), "NOT_STARTED" | "IN_PROGRESS" | "COMPLETED" | "FAILED")`) with no mechanical binding to the reviewed vendor enum ProfilingStatusFilter (contracts/vendor/red-team-management/0.86.0/openapi.json:5300-5307). Every data-plane list filter instead validates declared query values through contract.json via common::current_query (e.g. scans.rs:151). No tool or test compares this literal set with the vendor enum: tools/red_team_management.py only hash-binds the whole file and requires the two test names (lines 616-617, 664-667). An upstream enum extension fails closed as an unreviewed delta, but once a maintainer registers that delta's hash the SDK would keep rejecting the newly declared value with no check failing, and conversely a typo'd literal here would not be detected by any source-bound check.
findings.required_fix: Bind the allowlist to the source: either generate the accepted values into a constant from the pinned spec (as tools/red_team_management_models.py already does for enum/union nodes), or add a check in tools/red_team_management.py that parses the literal set out of targets.rs and asserts equality with components.schemas.ProfilingStatusFilter.enum from the pinned mp-openapi.yaml, failing closed on any difference.

findings.description: The profiling_status rustdoc lists the four accepted filter values but does not record the documented filter inconsistency for response-only values: the plan (docs/red-team-management-0.86-plan.md:157-158) requires preserving PARTIALLY_COMPLETE and INIT response values and recording that no filter maps to them. PARTIALLY_COMPLETE is named in the status doc (line 26), but INIT is not mentioned in any public documentation of either field, so a caller seeing a response profiling_status of INIT or PARTIALLY_COMPLETE has no in-crate statement that those values cannot be filtered and must not be mapped to NOT_STARTED.
findings.required_fix: Extend the profiling_status rustdoc to state that responses may carry INIT and PARTIALLY_COMPLETE, that no filter value is declared for them, and that the SDK deliberately performs no mapping (mirroring the wording already used for the legacy status field).

findings.description: The end-to-end propagation test exercises only profiling_status=NOT_STARTED across the four collection surfaces. The remaining three accepted values (IN_PROGRESS, COMPLETED, FAILED) are covered only at the private query() level in the in-file unit test (targets.rs:404), so there is no wire evidence that every accepted value survives URL encoding and per-page closure cloning, and no wire case combines profiling_status with the other declared filters (adapter_uuid, target_type, search) to prove no key is dropped or duplicated across pages.
findings.required_fix: Parameterize profiling_filter_propagates_through_every_page_and_collection_surface over all four accepted values and include one case that sets adapter_uuid/target_type/search alongside both status and profiling_status, asserting the full decoded query map on every page.

evidence: crates/scm-sdk/src/airs/red_team/targets.rs:74-82 validates profiling_status against exactly NOT_STARTED|IN_PROGRESS|COMPLETED|FAILED and returns ErrorKind::Validation otherwise; this is byte-identical to the pinned vendor domain in contracts/vendor/red-team-management/0.86.0/openapi.json:5300-5307 (ProfilingStatusFilter) and to the reviewed decision rows in that directory's compatibility-decisions.json (lines 727-742).

targets.rs:23-36 carries the plan-mandated rustdoc on both fields: status is documented as legacy/transmitted unchanged with only DRAFT and ACTIVE still declared and FAILED, QUEUED, IN_PROGRESS, COMPLETED, PARTIALLY_COMPLETE named as no longer declared, plus the explicit 'service may reject' caveat (satisfying docs/red-team-management-0.86-plan.md:161-168).

Propagation is real, not asserted: targets.rs:341 pre-validates, targets.rs:343-357 clones the whole TargetListOptions into the Pages closure and only overwrites skip, and list_items/list_all (targets.rs:367-385) route through list_pages, so the filter reaches every page of all four surfaces.

Pre-auth rejection is proven by tests/red_team_management_contracts.rs:503-521, which for QUEUED, PARTIALLY_COMPLETE, "", FUTURE and ACTIVE asserts all four surfaces error and that provider.calls == 0 and wire.requests is empty — i.e. no token exchange and no dispatch.

tests/red_team_management_contracts.rs:451-501 asserts decoded query pairs per page across list/pages/items/all: profiling_status=NOT_STARTED and legacy status=QUEUED are present on every request with skip advancing per page, and replies are fully consumed.

In-file unit tests targets.rs:392-445 cover the cross-product of eight legacy status strings (including QUEUED, PARTIALLY_COMPLETE and an unknown 'future-status') with all four accepted profiling values, assert the exact emitted query vector, assert the default options produce an empty query, and reject "", INIT, QUEUED, PARTIALLY_COMPLETE, lowercase 'failed' and 'FAILED\n'.

Executed evidence (not prose): docs/reviews/phase-22-chunk-target-filtering-attempt-01.checks.json records passed: true with source_sha256 a5f303826de01da8434122faa798a005a981c4595a1e4fa0ec7808a7ad784881 matching the reviewed SHA, and every entry has exit_code 0 with non-trivial durations.

The same receipt contains four real scripts/check-rust.py runs (1.89.0 red-team 273.3 s, 1.99.0 red-team 123.6 s, 1.89.0 red-team+arbitrary_precision 285.8 s, 1.99.0 red-team+arbitrary_precision 297.7 s); each captured sub-command list includes cargo fmt --check, cargo check, clippy -D warnings, cargo test --workspace and cargo test --examples at exit_code 0, so the chunk's unit and integration tests executed under the red-team feature on MSRV 1.89 and the current pin.

tools/red_team_management.py --check --require-through-phase 22 passes in the receipt; tools/red_team_management.py:640-667 requires manifest adoption, verifies recorded SHA256 for each binding, and tokenizes the contracts test file to require the test names, and contracts/vendor/red-team-management/0.86.0/operations.json:3361-3366,3384-3385 records the targets.rs and contracts-test digests plus profiling_filter_propagates_through_every_page_and_collection_surface and invalid_profiling_filter_never_acquires_token_or_dispatches.

Chunk scope matches the declaration exactly: docs/phase-status.json:5618-5634 declares target-filtering with scope_evidence of precisely crates/scm-sdk/src/airs/red_team/targets.rs and crates/scm-sdk/tests/red_team_management_contracts.rs, and the chunk is still 'pending' with no prior reviews (attempt 1/5 is consistent).

Architectural consistency: the eager pre-validation pattern in list_pages mirrors the existing crates/scm-sdk/src/airs/red_team/scans.rs:151, and status reuses crates/scm-sdk/src/airs/red_team/common.rs:87-93 filter(), so no legacy value is narrowed (only >4096 bytes or control characters are refused, as before).

Secret-safety: targets.rs:38 applies redacted_debug! to TargetListOptions, the invalid-filter error carries no value, and the chunk's transport stub (tests/red_team_management_contracts.rs:297) asserts the synthetic secret never appears in request Debug output.

No compatibility break from the new field: TargetListOptions is #[non_exhaustive] with Default (targets.rs:15-17), so external construction already required Default/field assignment, which is exactly how the integration test builds it (lines 459-462).
limitations: Read-only review: I could not execute cargo, python or node, and could not recompute SHA256 digests. Acceptance of the executed-check claims rests on docs/reviews/phase-22-chunk-target-filtering-attempt-01.checks.json whose recorded source_sha256 equals the reviewed SHA supplied in the prompt and whose entries carry exit codes, captured stdout/stderr and durations consistent with real execution.

docs/checks/phase-22-private-material.json is bound to the same source SHA, but the receipt-verification run in the chunk evidence reports privateScanReexecuted: false — the credential scan itself was executed earlier (checkedAt 14:31:47Z) and only its freshness/structure was re-verified at check time (14:50Z). No credential or tenant-registration file was opened during this review.

verify-contracts.py reports extractedBaselineVerified: false in the no-baseline run and excludedRemoteBytesVerified: false in both runs; these are pre-existing boundaries of the frozen-baseline check and outside this chunk's scope, so I did not re-audit them.

I judged only the target-filtering chunk. The union/overlay/model artifacts (contracts/red-team-management-*.json, crates/scm-sdk/src/models/**, validation/schema_graph.json) belong to the connection-compatibility and typed-connections chunks; I inspected them only far enough to confirm the vendor filter domain, that response enums stay open (NOT_STARTED appears in schema_graph.json, not as a named Rust variant), and that this chunk does not depend on unimplemented later-phase work. Operations marked planned for phases 23-25 were not treated as missing deliverables.

Live/tenant acceptance is explicitly out of scope: all evidence here is offline. The receipt's qualification output shows liveVerified 0 and liveNotVerified 448, consistent with the phase 22 offline boundary, so nothing in this review certifies that the service accepts or rejects any particular filter value.
